In less than a year, the new tank has developed a crack in the same place. We are hoping that there might be someone at the university (senior millwright possibly) with expertise with air compressors who could look at our current set-up as well as these options and offer another opinion.  Having 2 tanks crack suggests there is an issue with the size or set-up, however we don't want to purchase a new and expensive rotary screw air compressor if there is some inherent issue that will cause it to fail as well.    Our digester is shut down until we can refurnish the current compressor or purchase a new one and we badly need to use it, so this is an urgent request.  Please contact me (Betty at 220-2806) if you have questions or need more information.  Thanks.

I've lived in Crowsnest Hall continuously for the past 12 months and this is my 3rd apartment, so I have a slight idea of how the HVAC system is supposed to work. In the first apartment I stayed in (number 309), I had an HVAC incident that lasted from Dec 2015 to Jan 2016. From that experience and from the questions I was asked by maintenance staff back then, here are some details about my current problem that might be relevant:  1. Crowsnest Hall has thermostats that can be set between 13C and 35C, and I am aware that residents don't have much control over the temperature and can only change it between 18C and 24C.  2. I am in a studio and my entire apartment has 1 thermostat.  3. For the past two weeks, the temperature in my room has been 22C, regardless of what I set the thermostat to. On rare occasions, it went to 21C and 23C, but for 95% of the time, it has been stuck at 22C.   4. I know 22C is a bearable temperature and meets the requirement of your service level agreement (even though I find it slightly cold), but I find it very strange that it is not changing, given that the previous two apartments I stayed in at Crowsnest Hall were significantly warmer.   5. I have had my thermostat set at 25C and not over 30C because I know that setting it at a high temperature can cause the heating to shut off.  6. On two occasions, I tried turning off the heating by setting the thermostat at the lowest setting for an hour or two, then turning it back up again. The issue was not solved (and surprisingly, the temperature did not go below 22C, so there might be an AC problem as well, but I prefer my room warm, so the heating problem is much more important to me at this point).  7. In my past two apartments, I was able to hear the slightly robotic sound of the controller in my heating panel turning on and off every couple of hours. Also, whenever I touched the ceiling heating panel that contains the hot water pipes in my old apartments, it was always warm. So far, for the past two weeks, I have never heard the controller sound and the panel has been cold the entire time, so **I CAN GUARANTEE THAT NO HOT WATER HAS BEEN CIRCULATING IN THE HEATING PANEL FOR THE PAST 14 DAYS** (ever since I moved in).  8. I briefly mentioned earlier that I had a similar problem in my old apartment (#309) in December 2015. Everything I've written so far has been identical to what I faced back then (except that the temperature was much colder in my room because it was winter). After around 22 days and several visits from maintenance in Dec/Jan, the way that problem was solved was by going to the room above me on the top floor (#709) and opening the valve in their heating panel to run hot water through the pipes in that apartment. That solved the problem in my room, and I was told by maintenance that the people above me (apartments 409, 509, and 609) might have all had the sample problem too since my hot water pipes were very cold.  9. So, a possible solution for my current problem might be opening the hot water valve inside the heating panel of apartment 702 because **I have asked the person living in apartment 602, and they are facing the same problem as me**; therefore, this might be happening in all the apartments ending in 02.  SUMMARY: My room temperature is 22C and not changing, and the heating panel is cold, which means that there is no hot water circulation in my heater. A possible solution might be forcing the hot water to circulate in the apartment above me since that solution worked when I was facing a similar problem 8 months ago. So, could someone please come and investigate? Thanks a lot!  Sincerely,  Taha (403 998 8277)
